gap: No result ChatGPT got names a charger for the case it raised itself, a single 24V or 36V LiFePO4 trolling battery: Minn Kota PCL and NOCO GENPRO are 12V-per-bank only, while Redodo sells a 29.2V 20A charger for 24V packs ($109.99) and a 43.8V 25A IP65 charger for 36V packs ($149.99), and Dakota Lithium sells 28.8V 10A ($60) and 43.2V 8A ($100) chargers.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited Minn Kota help pages (PCL Features/Specs and the Battery Charger Selection Guide) and the uncited 'Using the PCL' page. They say Minn Kota chargers are '12 Volt battery systems only' and 'not compatible with single 24V and 36V Lithium Batteries', so rivals cover the exclusion. None of them names a charger that does work. ChatGPT's own answer stops at 'requires a charger specifically compatible with that voltage'. The cited no.co GENPRO10X3 specs page returned 403 to me, and gearranking.com/marine-chargers/lithium/ failed on a certificate error, so I could not check those two. This rating assumes neither names a 29.2V or 43.x V charger.
decides: It splits the pick by battery setup. With separate 12V batteries (one per bank), multi-bank 12V onboard chargers stay the picks: NOCO GENPRO10X3 Lithium mode 14.6V and Minn Kota PCL max 14.5V. Both sit inside Redodo's 14.4V ±0.2V 12V LiFePO4 window. With one single 24V or 36V LiFePO4 pack, every charger ChatGPT listed is excluded. The shopper needs a single-output charger matched to the pack's voltage, such as Redodo 29.2V 20A / 43.8V 25A or Dakota 28.8V / 43.2V, and should use the battery maker's own charger because Redodo (2×/3×14.6V) and Dakota (2×/3×14.4V) use different setpoints.
